NONE: A1 used to refer to the person or people being spoken or written to
你；您；你們
A2 people in general
（泛指）你，任何人

example: You look nice.
你看起來不錯。
I love you.
我愛你。
You said I could go with you.
你說過我可以和你一起去。
You're coming tonight, aren't you?
你今晚會過來，對嗎?
Are you two ready?
你倆準備好了嗎？
You painted that yourself? That's great!
那個是你自己畫的？太棒了！
You learn to accept these things as you get older.
年紀大些之後，你開始學會接受這些事情。
You can't get a driving licence till you're 17 in this country.
在這個國家，17歲以下人士不能獲得駕駛執照。
Too much alcohol is bad for you.
飲酒過量對身體有害。
How do you get this thing to start?
怎樣才能令這東西啟動？

NONE: › used to emphasize a statement or to mean "certainly"
（表示強調）當然
› US used when someone thanks you
（回應對方的感謝時）不用謝

example: "Are you coming to the party?" "You bet!"
「你來參加派對嗎？」「當然了。」

NONE: › used to say that you are completely certain that something is true or will happen
肯定

example: You can bet your bottom dollar that she'll be the next president.
她肯定會當選下一任總統。

NONE: › used to emphasize that you can make it easy for someone to do something, but you cannot force them to do it
牽馬到河邊容易，逼馬飲水難。（意指為他人做某事創造條件易，使其做某事難。）
› used to show that you completely agree with what someone has said
你說得很對！一點也沒錯！
› said to show that you cannot know what something or someone is like by looking only at that person or thing's appearance
勿只憑外表判斷；不能以貌取人
› used to mean that you cannot make something good out of something that is naturally bad
劣材難成器；朽木不可雕也
› it is hard to achieve something important without causing unpleasant effects
不打破雞蛋就攤不成蛋餅；有失才有得
› used to say that you cannot make something without the necessary materials
巧婦難為無米之炊
› used to say that you think an offer or arrangement is good
價格再公道不過了；協定的條件已很優厚了
› said to mean that it is very difficult to teach someone new skills or to change someone's habits or character
年老難學藝；本性難移
› something you say that means it is not possible to succeed at everything you do
不可能凡事都成功；有得必有失

example: It would have been great to get the job but I suppose you can't win 'em all.
能得到那份工作就好了，但是不可能事事都如意的。

NONE: › you can be certain
可以肯定

example: You haven't heard the last of this, depend upon it.
你還不知道此事的最新消息，這一點是可以肯定。

NONE: › used to describe a situation in which everyone is feeling very angry or nervous and you feel that something unpleasant could soon happen
（局面）劍拔弩張，一觸即發
› something that you say in order to describe a situation where there was complete silence, especially because people were very interested or very surprised by what was happening
（因著迷或驚訝而）鴉雀無聲

example: Margaret's ex-husband turned up at the wedding. Honestly, you could have heard a pin drop.
瑪格麗特的前夫出現在婚禮現場。老實說，當時全場真是鴉雀無聲。

NONE: › said when you are extremely surprised
（用來表示自己極度吃驚）你嚇死我了！
› used either to express surprise or lack of surprise in a humorous and slightly unkind way
（表示驚訝）不會這樣吧！不至於吧！（幽默且不太客氣地表示並不驚訝）我就知道！

example: "He's lost his job." "You don't say!"
「他丟掉了工作。」「不會吧！」

NONE: › used to say that you will quickly do what someone has asked you to do
（用於表示很快就完成對方要求你做的事情）

example: "Would you get me a coffee?" "Sure, you got it!"
「你能幫我拿杯咖啡麼？」「沒問題，馬上就來。」

NONE: › informal also you must be kidding used to show that you are very surprised by what someone has said and do not accept it
（表示對某人的話非常驚訝而且不相信是真的）別開玩笑了

example: You want me to drive into the city? You’ve got to be kidding.
你想讓我開車去城裡？別開玩笑了。

NONE: › said for emphasis when you are describing how good or bad an experience is
（表示強調）你不知道，你難以想像

example: Flying a plane is wonderful, you have no idea.
你不知道駕駛飛機有多棒。
You have no idea how embarrassed I was.
你不知道我當時有多尷尬。

NONE: B1 a phrase with little meaning, used while you are trying to think of what to say next
（用於話語銜接）你知道嗎
B1 used when trying to help someone remember something or when trying to explain something
（用於提醒或解釋）你知道

example: Well I just thought, you know, I'd better agree to it.
嗯，你知道嗎，我想我最好同意此事。
I'm not happy with the situation but, you know, there isn't much I can do about it.
我對這情況也不滿意，但你知道嗎，我對此也做不了甚麼。
What's the name of that guy on TV - you know, the one with the silly voice?
電視裡那個人叫甚麼——你知道的，那個說話聲音很怪的人？

NONE: › said before giving an opinion or a piece of information
（用於告知意見或資訊之前）要我告訴你嗎？你聽說了嗎？

example: You know something? I don't think I like that man.
聽我說，我想我不喜歡那個人。
You know what? I think it's time to go home.
要我告訴你嗎？我想該回家了。

NONE: › said when you hear or discover something that is surprising
（表示對得知的東西感到驚訝）真想不到

example: I had no idea they were related. Oh well, you live and learn.
我一點都沒想到他們之間還有聯繫。唉，真是想不到啊。

NONE: › it would be very interesting to know
（表示…耐人尋味）你覺得出奇吧

example: How could Jonathan afford to buy a new car? You may well ask.
喬納森怎麼買得起新車的呢？你感到出奇吧？

NONE: › said to mean that because the punishment for a bad action and an even worse one will be the same, you have no reason not to do the worse one
既然懲罰都一樣，我還不如索性做得更差些。
B1 said in answer to something that someone has said, meaning that you do not believe they need said it seriously, or you think it is a stupid thing to say
（表示不相信或覺得荒謬）你一定是在開玩笑吧

example: You've got to be joking if you think I'm going to stand in the rain watching you play tennis!
你以為我會站在雨中看你打網球，你一定是在開玩笑吧！

NONE: C2 used to say there are many things to choose from
凡是你說得出的；應有盡有

example: Gin, vodka, whisky, beer - you name it, I've got it.
杜松子酒、伏特加、威士卡、啤酒——隨你點，我這兒都有。
I've tried every diet going - you name it, I've tried it.
我嘗試過各種節食方法——只要你說得出的，我都試過。

NONE: B2 said to mean there is a possibility that something good might happen, even if it is slight
很難說，很難預料

example: You never know, she might change her mind.
很難說，她或許會改變想法。

NONE: › said to someone who must decide between different things and accept the results of their decision
你就碰碰運氣吧。
› You are responsible for your decisions and cannot blame anyone else when what you have chosen is not successful.
自己選擇自己承擔後果。
› used to say that you agree with what has just been said
你說對了！正是如此！沒錯！

example: "How stupid of me to lend him that money!" "You said it!"
「我借錢給他，真傻。」「沒錯！」

NONE: › used to tell someone that if they help you, you will help them
你幫我，我也幫你；我們互謀其利
C1 used when you hope someone else will understand what you are saying or asking
你看；你知道

example: You see, it's better if you do your homework before dinner.
你看，如果你在晚飯前把功課完成了就更好。
You see, I'm one of those people who likes to try new things.
你知道，我就是那種喜歡嘗試新東西的人。

NONE: › used to say that someone is very unlikely to get what they want
（用於告訴某人其幾乎不可能如願）但願你走運！

example: "She's going to ask for a salary increase." "She should be so lucky!"
「她打算要求加薪。」「但願她走運吧！」

NONE: › used to tell someone that they are spending too much time doing things that are boring or not important
你應該做點更有意義的事；別老憋在家裡做些雞毛蒜皮的事

example: "I arranged all my CDs in alphabetical order." "Mmm, I think you should get out more, Mike."
「我把所有的光碟都按字母順序排好了。」「哦，我覺得你倒不如出去做些更有意思的事，麥克。」

NONE: › seeing or hearing something or someone would have interested or entertained you very much
你真該看看／聽聽（某事或某人）

example: You should have seen her - she was furious!
你真該看看她那時的模樣——她大發脾氣！

NONE: › said when thanking someone who has given you a present, to mean that you did not expect it
（當別人給你禮物時，用來表示你沒有期待如此）

example: Flowers! You shouldn't have!
「給我的鮮花！你不必送的！」

NONE: › if you do not pay attention and do something quickly, someone else will do it instead of you
一旦不留神就會被人搶先
› used to praise a person who has done something well
（用於稱讚）做得不錯，老兄！真有你的！
› something you say to someone who has persuaded you to do something that you did not intend to do, especially when that person has used force and you are angry
（好吧）你贏了！（用於表示被說服，尤指對方使用強制辦法時）

example: Okay, you win - you can go to the party! But you'd better be home by midnight!
好了，你贏了——你可以去參加這個聚會！不過最好半夜前回來！

NONE: › short form of you had
（you had的縮略形式）
› short form of you would
（you would的縮略形式）

example: It happened just after you'd left the room.
你剛離開房間，事情就發生了。
You'd be much warmer in your black jacket.
你穿上那件黑色的外套會暖和很多。

NONE: › short form of you will
（you will的縮略形式）

example: You'll remember to tell her, won't you?
你會記得告訴她，對吧？

NONE: › short form of you are
（you are的縮略形式）

example: You're so nice to me!
你對我真是太好了！

NONE: › something you say to someone when they have been nice and helpful to you
（表示感激某人）你真是個大好人！
› said by children playing a guessing or searching game to tell the person who is guessing or searching that he or she is getting further away from the answer or hidden object
（兒童遊戲時用語）你距離（答案或目標）更遠了；你猜得越來越離譜了
› used to show that you think that what someone has just said is not reasonable or fair
你在開玩笑

example: £500 to cut down a tree - you're having a laugh, mate!
500英鎊砍一棵樹——老兄，你簡直是在開玩笑！

NONE: B1 something you say to show that you are surprised by what someone has said, or do not believe it is true
（表示吃驚或不相信）你是在開玩笑吧！

example: "Hey, Maria's leaving." "You're joking!"
「嘿，瑪麗亞要走了。」「你在開玩笑吧！」

NONE: › used as a way of expressing agreement to something happening
（表示贊同）好！行！

example: "I'll give you £50 for your bike." "You're on!"
「我出50英磅買你的腳踏車。」「成交！」

NONE: › used to say that you strongly agree with what someone has just said
那還用說！你說的太對了！

example: "Stephen's in such a bad mood today." "You're telling me!"
「斯蒂芬今天心情很不好。」「那還用說！」

NONE: A2 said as a polite answer when someone thanks you for doing something
（用於回答別人的感謝）別客氣，不用謝

example: "Thank you so much for helping." "You're welcome."
「非常感謝你的幫助。」「別客氣。」

NONE: › short form of you have
（you have的縮略形式）

example: You've dropped something.
你掉了什麼東西。

NONE: › used to say that you cannot make things worse, or cause any disadvantages for yourself by doing a particular thing
不會有任何損失；不會有任何壞處

example: Why don't you take the job? You've got nothing to lose.
你為甚麽不接受這份工作？這對你不會有任何壞處。

NONE: › said when you can see something funny in a difficult situation
還是值得一笑，還有可笑之處
› said to someone who must accept the unpleasant results of something they have done
自食其果，自作自受
› used for telling someone that when they consider all the facts and figures, something cannot succeed or be possible
你自己算算（表示讓人自己考慮各種因素，並得出結論）
› used when you think that the person listening understands and so you do not need to say any more
（你）懂我的意思

example: You've got to give him a chance, you know what I mean?
你得給他一個機會，你明白我的意思吧？

NONE: › something that you say when you tell someone about something that you are certain will happen in the future
（告訴別人某事將來肯定會發生時用語）（你）記住我的話！

example: He'll cause trouble - you mark my words!
他會惹麻煩的——你記住我的話！

NONE: y'all
A1 having lived or existed for only a short time and not old
幼小的；年輕的
› suitable for young people
（適合）年輕人的
› to look younger than you really are
顯得比實際年齡年輕
B2 young people considered together as a group
（總稱）青年人，年輕人
› the babies of an animal
幼鳥；幼獸；幼崽

example: His girlfriend's very young.
他的女朋友非常年輕。
The trees in this part of the forest are still fairly young.
森林中的這一片樹木還沒長大。
Philippa is the youngest person in the family.
菲莉帕是家裡最小的。
Angela is two years younger than Clare.
安傑拉比克萊爾小兩歲。
Be honest now - do you think this dress is a bit/too young for me (= is more suitable for someone younger)?
說實話——你覺不覺得這件衣服對我來說有點／太年輕？
I have nothing against miniskirts, but I think they're strictly for the young.
我並不反對穿迷你裙，但我認為它們只適合年輕人。
Meanwhile, the mother flies back to the nest to feed her young.
其間，母鳥會飛回巢中給雛鳥餵食。

NONE: › thinking and behaving as if you are younger than you really are
心態年輕

example: Dad may be nearly 90 but he's still young at heart.
爸爸可能年近90了，但他心態依然很年輕。

NONE: › young people who have a lot of energy and ideas
新鮮血液（指充滿活力、思想活躍的年輕人）

example: We need to introduce more young blood into the organization.
我們需要為組織注入更多新鮮血液。

NONE: › used when you are speaking angrily to a young person
（用於氣憤地對年輕人說話）
› old-fashioned or humorous someone's girlfriend or boyfriend
女朋友；男朋友

example: Mind your language, young lady!
注意你的用詞，小姐！
If you would bring your young man along too, we would be delighted to meet him.
如果你願意把男朋友帶來，我們很高興見見他。

NONE: › love between young people
年輕人的愛情
› a special place for people who have done bad things and are too young to be sent to prison
少年犯管教所
C1 a young person, usually an older child
年輕人；少年
A1 belonging or relating to the person or group of people being spoken or written to
你的；您的；你們的
B1 belonging or relating to people generally
（泛指）你的，任何人的
› informal said before a typical example of something is given
（用在典型事例前）（你們）常說的

example: Is this your bag?
這是你的袋子嗎？
It's not your fault.
這不是你的錯。
Your mother is driving me crazy.
你母親快把我逼瘋了。
What's your problem?
你怎麼了？
Of course you want the best for your children.
當然人人都希望給自己的孩子們最好的。
Garlic is good for your blood.
大蒜對血液有益。
This isn't your usual science fiction novel, but then Brinkworth isn't exactly your typical author.
這並非我們常說的科幻小說，而布林克沃思也不完全是我們說的那種典型作家。

NONE: › the sleep that you need in order to feel and look healthy and attractive
美容覺
› your best clothes that you wear on special occasions
最漂亮的衣服
› your main advantage over other people
絕妙高招，撒手鐧，王牌
› something that you say to someone who is being talked about
（因爲被人議論）耳根發熱，發窘

example: All this talk about Emma - her ears must be burning!
聽聽大家這個議論啊——艾瑪耳朵不發熱才怪！

NONE: › a way of describing the way you look when you are extremely surprised to see something or someone
（表示驚奇）眼睛瞪得都要掉出來了

example: When she saw the amount written on the cheque, her eyes nearly popped out of her head.
當她看到支票上的數字時，她的眼珠子瞪得都快要掉出來了。

NONE: › something you say when you do not know the answer to a question
我跟你一樣也不知道

example: "What's he doing?" "Your guess is as good as mine."
「他在做甚麼啊？」「我也不知道。」

NONE: › If your heart aches, you feel sad or feel sympathy and sadness for the suffering of other people.
（爲他人的痛苦）感到心痛，非常傷心

example: His heart ached with pity for her.
他深深地同情她。

NONE: › If your heart goes out to someone who is in trouble, you feel sympathy for them.
對…深感同情

example: Our hearts go out to the families of the victims of this terrible tragedy.
我們對這場可怕悲劇的受害者家庭深表同情。

NONE: › If your heart isn't in it, you do not feel interested or enthusiastic about something.
心思不在…上面，對…不感興趣

example: I tried to look interested, but my heart wasn't in it.
我試圖裝出感興趣的樣子，可是我的心思完全不在這上面。

NONE: › When your heart skips/misses a beat, you feel very excited or nervous.
（表示興奮或緊張）心跳停了一拍，心裡一陣緊張

example: Every time he looks at me my heart skips a beat.
他每看我一眼，我的心裡就一陣緊張。

NONE: › the thing or person you most want
最想得到的東西（或人）
› If you think your hour has come, you think you are going to die.
（某人）死期將近

example: I thought my hour had come when he pointed his gun at me.
當他用槍指著我時，我想我的死期到了。

NONE: › what you consider to be something
（某人）心目中的…

example: Playing card games is not my idea of fun.
我並不認為玩紙牌很有趣。
Is this your idea of a joke? (= Do you think that this is amusing?)
你覺得這好笑嗎？

NONE: › a person who has authority over you, or your husband
主人；老闆；丈夫
› used to tell someone that they have been lucky or successful
你要走桃花運了！

example: He's been looking at you all evening - I think your luck's in, Cath.
他一晚上都在看你——我覺得你要走桃花運了，凱思。

NONE: › informal humorous your mental health or your ability to think and remember clearly
精神健康；思考和記憶能力

example: I think he's losing his marbles (= starting to forget things or become crazy).
我認為他腦子開始出問題了。
She's 89, but she's still got all her marbles.
她已89歲，但頭腦非常清楚。

NONE: › When your mind is a blank/goes blank, you cannot remember a particular thing, or you cannot remember anything.
腦海裡一片空白；記不起

example: I tried to remember her name, but my mind was a complete blank/went completely blank.
我努力想記起她的名字，但腦袋裡一片空白。

NONE: › When your mind is on something, you think about it or give attention to it.
心思在…上

example: I couldn't concentrate on my work - my mind was on other things.
我無法集中精神工作——我的心思在別的事情上。
My mind wasn't on what he was saying, so I missed half of it.
我的心思並不在他所說的話上，所以恐怕漏聽了一半的內容。

NONE: › If your name is mud, other people are angry with you because of something you have said or done.
名譽掃地

example: If he doesn't turn up tonight, his name will be mud.
如果他今晚不出現的話，他將聲名狼藉。

NONE: › your family, especially those that you live with or are very involved with
至親，至愛
› When your number is up, you are going to die.
（某人）氣數已盡，死到臨頭

example: When the plane started to shake, I just thought my number was up.
飛機開始搖晃時，我真的以為我要完蛋了。

NONE: › your family or relations
自己的骨肉；自己的親人（或親戚）

example: It's hard to believe that he could treat his own flesh and blood so badly.
真難相信，他對自己的親生骨肉會這麼狠。

NONE: › used to say that you will not tell anyone what you have just been told
我會守口如瓶的

example: "I'd appreciate it if you kept quiet about this." "Don't worry - your secret's safe with me."
「如果你對此保密，我將非常感謝。」「放心，我會守口如瓶。」

NONE: › your spoken opinion on a particular matter
（某人的）意見，想法，觀點

example: I thought I'd just throw in (= add) my two cents' worth.
我想只談談我個人的想法。

NONE: › If someone's word is their bond, they always keep a promise.
總是信守諾言

example: "But listen, you have to promise never to tell anyone." "My word is my bond."
「聽著，你必須保證不告訴任何人。」「我一向信守諾言。」

NONE: › the money that you need so that you can pay for food, clothes, and other ordinary needs
維持生計所需的錢

example: He earns his daily bread as a tourist guide.
他靠做導遊謀生。

NONE: › everything that you do
一舉一動；做的每一件事

example: I'd hate to be someone really famous with the press reporting my every move.
那種一舉一動都被登上報紙的大名人我才不願意當。

NONE: › used to mean "you", when addressing a group of people that you are speaking to

S or U: B2 [ S or U ] the period of your life when you are young, or the state of being young
